notes.title: DEVLOG #5 - Producing
notes.notes:
[p]A little-known secret in the world of game development is the crucial role producers play in bringing a game to life. Many players may not realize how essential they are to ensuring a game’s excellence, so we want to take a moment to shine a spotlight on our producers and explain why they’re absolutely vital to our success!

A huge thank you to [b]Micke[/b] and [b]Guillaume[/b], our incredible producers at Dotemu, and to [b]Matéo[/b] at Supamonks, who expertly handled the art production with dedication and care.[/p][p][/p][h3]COORDINATION IS KEY[/h3][p]At its core, the producer’s job is all about coordination. For example, how do you create a new character for the game? Every step must be carried out in the right order. Here's a simplified breakdown of how studios typically approach this process:[/p][olist][*][p][b]Game Design[/b] – The initial concept for the character is written.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Concept Art[/b] – Visual designs are created.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Animations[/b] – The character’s movements are brought to life.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Code Integration[/b] – The character is implemented into the game.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Sound Design[/b] – Voices and sound effects are added.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Testing[/b] – Everything is tested to ensure it functions correctly.[/p][/*][/olist][p]In this process alone, [b]at least six people[/b] from different disciplines are involved in the creation of a single character or enemy. The producer’s job is to ensure that each team member performs at their best and that the final result meets the highest standards of quality.[/p][p][/p][h3]FOCUSING ON QUALITY[/h3][p]As a game designer, it’s critical to have the freedom to focus on your core expertise. If you’re bogged down with budget calculations, scouting freelance partners, or managing the sound list, you can’t devote the attention needed to your craft. This is where the producer steps in, taking care of all the side tasks so that the design team can stay focused on what they do best.[/p][p][/p][h3]PREPARING FOR THE FUTURE[/h3][p]A great producer always keeps an eye on the future. They ensure that upcoming milestones (development checkpoints) are clearly defined and understood by everyone on the team. [/p][p]Developing a game is a marathon, not a sprint, and these milestones help break the process into manageable stages. The whole team needs to know exactly what they need to do to hit each checkpoint and keep the game moving forward.[/p][p][/p][h3]What Makes Absolum’s Production So Special?[/h3][p]Absolum is a monumental project—packed with content and high expectations for quality from Dotemu. We aim for it to be a standout title in our long history of beat 'em up productions. That’s why we’ve carefully chosen only the best talent for the job: the best designers, the best programmers, the best artists, the best musicians, and the best project managers.[/p][p]Managing a game with multiple studios involved presents its own set of challenges. Different work cultures, different visions, and different structures all need to be harmonized. Throughout this process, I’ve worked hard to inspire a sense of unity within the team. Whether it was through day-to-day collaboration or the use of management tools, we communicated openly, worked on Slack, and did our best to avoid becoming isolated or working in silos.[/p][p][/p][h3]HANDS-ON WORK WITH THE ENGINE[/h3][p]Supamonks played a crucial role in mastering the engine. They took a hands-on approach to learning how to implement and optimize the engine for the best possible animation sprites. Over time, they became almost fully independent in working with the engine for art production. Even our background artist, Manuel Tanon-Tchi, consistently amazed us by introducing new features that further elevated the game.[/p][p][/p][h3]A SYMPHONY OF NARRATIVE AND ART[/h3][p]When it came to worldbuilding, narrative and art had to work together in perfect harmony. It was a truly collaborative, two-way process. Our artists brought their creative ideas to the table, which in turn inspired the writers to explore new character nuances and backstories. This exchange of ideas enriched the narrative and led to exciting new visual concepts that seamlessly integrated into the story. The result? A game world that feels alive and interconnected, where every detail serves a purpose.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you for reading and see you next time for a new devlog![/p][p]The Absolum Team.[/p]

notes.title: DEVLOG #4 - NARRATIVE DESIGN
notes.notes:
[p]Narrative design is at the heart of what makes [i]Absolum[/i] so compelling, and we’ve made it our mission to tell a rich and immersive story, weaving intricate lore into our beat 'em up to bring [i]Absolum[/i]’s world to life in new ways![/p][p]But how do we convey this world to you, the player? Who’s behind it all? Let’s take a closer look![/p][p][/p][h3]NARRATION IN ABSOLUM[/h3][p]In [i]Absolum[/i], players will uncover the game’s rich narrative through a variety of sources. Whether it’s reading lore, listening to character dialogue, or simply interacting with the environment – every detail serves to immerse you deeper into the world.
[/p][p][u][b]Discovering Talamh[/b][/u][/p][p]Every run you make in [i]Absolum[/i] is an opportunity to uncover new aspects of the game’s lore. We’ve designed it so that at least something new would be revealed every time you play, at least during your first 50 runs. [/p][p]As you explore, you'll uncover hidden paths, encounter new NPCs, and discover secret areas. Many of the game’s quests require you to progress across multiple runs, rewarding you for persistent exploration and curiosity. The narrative structure is designed to keep you moving forward, always offering something new, whether that’s delving deeper into known locations or discovering entirely new places and characters.[/p][p][/p][p][u][b]An Evolving World[/b][/u][/p][p]The world of [i]Absolum[/i] isn’t static, it reacts to your actions. We don’t want to give too much away about this, but know that your decisions will influence how the world evolves, shifting both the challenges you face and the opportunities available to you.[/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Safe Spots[/b][/u][/p][p]Throughout the game, you’ll encounter safe spots to rest, hire mercenaries, or accept new quests. These safe spots are teeming with life, and you can talk to a variety of different characters there – every safe spot features its own custom art and layout![/p][p][/p][p][u][b]Dialogues & Secrets[/b][/u][/p][p]NPCs are more than just quest-givers—they hold intriguing insights into the world of Talamh. Some offer alternative perspectives on the ongoing conflict, while others might reveal quests tied to hidden storylines. Every character has a story, and if you dig deep enough, you’ll unlock secrets that give you exclusive rewards and new paths to explore.
[/p][p][u][b]2 players[/b][/u] [/p][p]In [i]Absolum[/i], even the dialogues change based on which character you’re playing in multiplayer. This adds an extra layer of depth, making the experience even more engaging when you team up with a friend.[/p][p][/p][h3]UNDERSTANDING THE PROCESS[/h3][p][u][b]The Challenges of Narrative Design[/b][/u][/p][p]Creating a narrative that fits into a fast-paced beat ‘em up was no small feat. We wanted to balance intricate lore with the fast rhythm of the game. Dialogue had to be sharp and concise, providing value without slowing down the action. The result? Short but impactful exchanges that enhance the experience without bogging down the pacing. In Absolum, you can expect dialogue that’s just as quick and punchy as the combat itself.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45526104/a9efee352a3fe8cbb66698c0aeada44941755ae9.png"][/img][/p][p][u][b]Pacing & Player Progression[/b][/u][/p][p]As you progress through the game, the story adapts to your journey. Whether you’ve played for 2 hours or 20, the narrative structure ensures that you always have access to essential information to understand the world and follow the plot. The Hub reflects your progress, and each decision shapes the unfolding story. This design ensures that both new players and veterans can enjoy the narrative at their own pace.[/p][p][/p][h3]WHO WORKED ON THE STORY?[/h3][p]The immersive world of Absolum is the result of a long and complex process. Three different narrative designers worked on the game:[/p][list][*][p][b]Matthew Ritter[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Fanny Renard[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Gautier Knittel[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]Each brought their unique vision and expertise to the project, shaping [i]Absolum [/i]into the world you’re about to experience. We’d like to take this moment to thank them for their dedication in crafting such a compelling and living world.[/p][p][/p][p]Stay tuned for more insights into the world of [i]Absolum [/i]in our upcoming devlogs. Until then, happy exploring![/p][p][/p][p]Cheers,[/p][p]The [b]Absolum[/b] Team. notes.title: DEVLOG #3 MEET THE COMPOSERS
notes.notes:
[p]The Absolum OST features an incredible lineup of composers, including Gareth Coker, Mick Gordon, Yuka Kitamura, and Motoi Sakuraba—a dream team that has come together to craft the perfect soundtrack for our game.
[/p][p][url="https://youtu.be/6aNBhvQh6Qs" style="button"]WATCH OUR COMPOSER DIARY![/url][/p][p][/p][p]At Dotemu, we’ve been fortunate to collaborate with one of the best partners in the industry: [b]Kid Katana Records[/b]. For years now, they’ve been instrumental in helping bring our projects to life, handling everything from the distribution of physical OST editions to connecting us with incredible talent. You might already recognize their work from titles like [i]Streets of Rage 4[/i] and [i]TMNT: Shredder's Revenge[/i].[/p][p]When we began developing [b]Absolum[/b], we knew we had to work with the best in the business. That’s where Tarafa and Rémy, the co-founders of KKR, came in. In their efforts in assembling the lineup for the [b]Absolum OST,[/b] they truly have outdone themselves, bringing together legendary names like [b]Gareth Coker[/b] ([i]Ori[/i], [i]Halo Infinite[/i], [i]Prince of Persia[/i]), [b]Yuka Kitamura[/b] ([i]Dark Souls[/i], [i]Elden Ring[/i]), [b]Mick Gordon[/b] ([i]DOOM Eternal[/i]), and [b]Motoi Sakuraba[/b] ([i]Golden Sun[/i], [i]Tales of...[/i]).
[/p][h3]Let’s Meet the Crew![/h3][p][b]Gareth Coker [/b]is our lead composer, and his role in shaping the overall sound of the game has been nothing short of essential. While we’re thrilled to have such extraordinary guest composers, it’s Gareth who has been the cornerstone of the entire score, ensuring that every note aligns perfectly with the world of Absolum.[/p][p][/p][p]Working with a composer of Gareth’s caliber can often lead to the temptation of reusing familiar themes, but with [i]Absolum [/i]being our first original IP and a bold reinvention of the beat ‘em up genre, we were committed to creating something entirely fresh. Under Gareth’s guidance, we ventured into uncharted musical territory, using the score not just to enhance the visuals, but to truly elevate the experience of gameplay.[/p][p][/p][p]Let us introduce you to the dream team:[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45526104/21c71b5b62140a0de32aa6f055b6fe8343093cdb.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Gareth Coker[/b] is a British composer known for his evocative and emotional video game soundtracks. He gained widespread recognition for his work on [i]Ori and the Blind Forest[/i] and its sequel, [i]Ori and the Will of the Wisps[/i]. His compositions blend orchestral grandeur with delicate, atmospheric melodies, creating immersive musical experiences. [/p][p]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45526104/37d74af78d42a5d90865a9c7144c21e6bd19399c.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Yuka Kitamura[/b] is a Japanese composer, best known for her work on FromSoftware’s [i]Dark Souls[/i] series, [i]Bloodborne[/i], and [i]Elden Ring[/i]. Her compositions blend haunting orchestral arrangements with intense, dramatic themes that heighten the tension and atmosphere of the games.[/p][p]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45526104/f9ba302722ba01c5875dd9c0ab21a5f35a1d26e4.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Mick Gordon[/b] is an Australian composer known for his intense and dynamic video game soundtracks. He gained worldwide recognition for his work on [i]DOOM[/i] (2016) and [i]DOOM Eternal[/i], where he fused heavy metal with electronic and industrial elements. [/p][p]
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45526104/5a190611069ea7e6a616782673f6b034e1dcea3b.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Motoi Sakuraba[/b] is a Japanese composer known for[i] Star Ocean[/i], [i]Golden Sun[/i] and [i]Dark Souls[/i]. His orchestral work has made JRPG history, going on to influence the entire video games industry.[/p][p][/p][h3]Crafting the Perfect Sound: A Challenge in Balance[/h3][p]Creating the music for [i]Absolum [/i]presented a unique challenge. With our game’s structure, we needed to strike the right balance between escalating intensity during combat while having moments to breathe in between. It was a lengthy process of playtesting, refining gameplay rhythms, and matching the tempo of the music to ensure everything flowed seamlessly.

What sets Gareth apart is his hands-on approach. For him, composing is more than just writing music—it’s about forging a deep connection with the game experience. He wasn’t just thinking about the visuals; he was focused on the feel of the gameplay, ensuring the music resonated with every aspect of the experience.[/p][p][/p][p]Gareth also understands the narrative power of music. He intentionally reintroduces key musical motifs at pivotal moments throughout the game, creating a sonic story that complements the gameplay and adds emotional depth to the journey.[/p][p][/p][h3]Collaborating with the Masters: How We Work with Our Composers[/h3][p]So, how does the collaboration work? Here’s a closer look:[/p][p][b]Gareth[/b] is the principal composer, crafting the majority of the soundtrack. He’s worked closely with our studio, ensuring that the music amplifies the atmosphere and emotional impact of each moment. Christophe Hogommat, the game’s sound designer, has been a crucial part of the process, collaborating with Gareth to ensure every sound and note is perfectly integrated into the game.[/p][p]On the guest composer side, [b]Sakuraba[/b], [b]Yuka[/b], and [b]Mick[/b] have each contributed unforgettable boss tracks, each layered with depth and intensity. Their music helps elevate those critical moments in the game—marking the dramatic shift in rhythm and reinforcing the epic nature of each boss fight. When these tracks hit, you’ll know it’s time for a legendary battle.[/p][p]And of course, a huge thank you to our sound designer, Christophe Hogommat. From sound creation to mixing and mastering, Christophe has been integral in bringing [i]Absolum[/i]’s[i] [/i]sound to life. His meticulous work behind the scenes ensures that the game’s audio enhances every aspect of gameplay.[/p][p][/p][p]We can’t wait for you to hear how these compositions come together in the game, but in the meantime… you can go listen to [i]Absolum’s [/i]first four singles available right now! (with more on the way!)[/p][p][/p][p]Cheers,
The [b]Absolum[/b] Team

notes.title: DEVLOG #2 – MEET THE PROGRAMMERS
notes.notes:
[p]Guard Crush Games and Dotemu have been partners for years, and we’re thrilled to continue working with them. Their contributions go far beyond simply programming the game. So, who exactly are they, and what role do they play in the development of Absolum?[/p][p] [/p][h3]About Guard Crush Games[/h3][p]Guard Crush Games is an independent game studio based in Montreal, renowned for their expertise in side-scrolling beat 'em up games. The studio was founded by a group of passionate developers with a deep love for classic arcade-style action games. They previously worked on [i]Streets of Fury[/i], a lesser-known but highly regarded beat 'em up featuring digitized character sprites.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45526104/04cf3bfe9817298a3af2d797c16df62b32f61114.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]What do they do on [i]Absolum[/i]?[/h3][p]Guard Crush is responsible for writing 100% of the code that powers Absolum. These talented programmers thrive on technical challenges, providing powerful editor tools and flexible code that’s perfect for game designers.[/p][p][/p][p]Their expertise extends beyond just coding. They play a crucial role in areas like UI design, game feel, and game inputs. Their contributions ensure that Absolum has a polished, responsive design that feels intuitive to players. Together with our designers, Guard Crush works hard to deliver the best gamepad experience possible, and we’re confident you’ll appreciate the effort.[/p][p][/p][p]They also know all there is to know about frames, identifying precisely what is required in order to offer the best combat experience, both in single-player and multiplayer modes. For example, latency can be a challenge: you want the game to feel smooth and responsive when playing with friends – something that several games struggle with![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45526104/c3be2a4d44590066c4d49f6c0efa2450462f5fb4.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]The Guard Crush Engine[/h3][p]Over the years Guard Crush has developed a powerful engine that is highly specialized in Beat ‘Em Ups, probably [i]the [/i]best-performing engine in the genre.[/p][p]In a world where many developers rely on Unity, this engine is a true gem. It allows us to push the boundaries of reactivity and intuitive game controls, something no competitor has access to. This is our secret weapon: the Guard Crush Games Engine.
[/p][p]For [i]Absolum[/i], Guard Crush had to design and build new tools to address the unique challenges of this beat 'em up, such as level verticality, precise hitboxes, and multiplayer synchronization. Some of these tools were carried over from previous games, and they will continue to be developed into the future! For instance, level design is crucial across all of our games, and the engine facilitates the process, enabling our level designers to tweak and alter every element to ensure the entire level is as compelling as possible.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45526104/dbe100eb63a756656db8f6d7c2fb425f80da2cad.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]A new challenge for Guard Crush with [i]Absolum[/i] was integrating roguelike elements. Coding for a roguelite requires exposing and balancing many variables: move speed, HP, dash effects, etc. Roguelikes are organized chaos: you need to be able to combine everything!
[/p][p]Tracking quests and mission progress was another new addition for Guard Crush. We need to ensure that all your game progress is recorded and organized properly across saves. The quests need to be properly registered, followed and organized in order to make sure none of your progress is lost.[/p][p][/p][p]There’s a lot to say about this engine, but we want to keep a few secrets as well, hehe…
[/p][p]A huge thank you to all the talented coders at Guard Crush for their dedication and hard work![/p][h3]
Play [i]Absolum[/i]'s Demo now![/h3][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3713610/Absolum_Demo/"][/dynamiclink]Your feedback is very valuable to us and for the game's future. So, please don't hesitate to share it with us on the Steam forums, our [url="https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fdiscord.com%2Finvite%2FRPxFsWMTdA"]official Discord[/url], or in a review![/p][p]We can't wait to hear your thoughts on Absolum✨[/p][p] [/p][h3]Join the rebellion by following us on social media and rise against the Sun King![/h3][list][*][p][url="https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fx.com%2FDotemu&snr=2___"]X - Dotemu[/url][/p][/*][*][p][url="https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Ftwitter.com%2FGuard_Crush&snr=2___"]X - Guard Crush Games[/url][/p][/*][*][p][url="https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fx.com%2Fsupamonks&snr=2___"]X - Supamonks[/url][/p][/*][*][p][url="https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Ftwitter.com%2FAbsolumGame&snr=2___"]X - Absolum[/url][/p][/*][*][p][url="https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.instagram.com%2Fabsolumgame%2F&snr=2___"]Instagram - Absolum[/url][/p][/*][*][p][url="https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.instagram.com%2Fdotemugames%2F&snr=2___"]Instagram - Dotemu[/url][/p][/*][*][p][url="https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.instagram.com%2Fsupamonksstudio%2F&snr=2___"]Instagram - Supamonks[/url][/p][/*][/list][p] And you can also find us on [url="https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.facebook.com%2Fgaming%2Fdotemu&snr=2___"]Facebook[/url], [url="https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.threads.net%2F%40dotemugames&snr=2___"]Threads[/url], [url="https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fbsky.app%2Fprofile%2Fdotemu.bsky.social&snr=2___"]Bluesky[/url], [url="https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tiktok.com%2F%40dotemu&snr=2___"]TikTok[/url], and on [url="https://discord.gg/RPxFsWMTdA"]Discord[/url]! notes.title: ABSOLUM: MEET THE ARTISTS
notes.notes:
[p]Our vibrant world would be nothing without its artists! Let’s meet them.[/p][p][/p][h3]What is Supamonks?[/h3][p]Supamonks is an [b]animation studio[/b] based in Paris, France. They’ve delivered amazing artistic work, in collaboration with our game and narrative designers. They were brought into the project very early on, and helped build the foundations of what Absolum is today! [/p][p]By producing all the art content throughout the game, they are absolutely vital to the production.[/p][p][/p][h3]Who worked on Absolum?[/h3][p]These are all the artists who have worked on Absolum (we hope we haven’t left anyone out!)
[/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=""][tr][th colspan="2"][p][b]Art Direction by Supamonks[/b][/p][/th][/tr][tr][th colspan="2"][p][b][i][u]SUPAMONKS[/u][/i][/b][/p][/th][/tr][tr][th][p]CEO[/p][/th][td][p]Julien Bagnol Roy[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Head of Studio [/p][/th][td][p]Annaelle Decaëns[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Art Director[/p][/th][td][p]Maxime Mary[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Main Producer[/p][/th][td][p]Matéo Boudras[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Producer[/p][/th][td][p]Azouz Menguellat[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Producer[/p][/th][td][p]Morgane Lemaire[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Lead animator[/p][/th][td][p]Leonard Bismuth[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Animator[/p][/th][td][p]Charles Badiller[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Animator[/p][/th][td][p]Suzon Heron[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Animator[/p][/th][td][p]Martin Hurmane[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Animator[/p][/th][td][p]Audrey Guibert[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Assistant animator[/p][/th][td][p]Julien Lin[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Assistant animator[/p][/th][td][p]Lucille Rizzo[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Assistant animator[/p][/th][td][p]Louise Boucher[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Lead environment artist[/p][/th][td][p]Manuel Tanon Tchi[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Environment artist[/p][/th][td][p]Leopold Gelbard[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Lead effects animator[/p][/th][td][p]Pierre Malenfant[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Effects animator[/p][/th][td][p]David Wegmann-Serin[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td colspan="2"][p][/p][/td][/tr][tr][th colspan="2"][p][b][i][u]SUPAMONKS - Additional Talent[/u][/i][/b][/p][/th][/tr][tr][th][p]Storyboard[/p][/th][td][p]Florent Remize[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Motion design[/p][/th][td][p]Robin Desnoue[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Environment support[/p][/th][td][p]Sebastien Iglesias[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Environment support[/p][/th][td][p]Hugo Pablo Moreno[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]3D support[/p][/th][td][p]Thibault Magrit[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]3D support[/p][/th][td][p]Simon Reynaud[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]3D support[/p][/th][td][p]Kimico Baeyens[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]2D support[/p][/th][td][p]Mehdi Tebbakh[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]2D support[/p][/th][td][p]Florent Thailhades[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Art Intern[/p][/th][td][p]Lauryne Grissin[/p][/td][/tr][tr][th][p]Art Intern[/p][/th][td][p]Camille Bardaud[/p][/td][/tr][/table][p]
Thank you to all of them, it’s almost impossible to showcase the vast amount of artwork that has gone into making the game what it is today.[/p][p][/p][h3]Art Direction[/h3][p]Maxime is our [b]Art Director[/b], everything goes through him. [/p][p]He’s responsible for the game looking as good as it possibly can. Obviously, he’s also a super-talented artist. He has dedicated countless hours to creating sprites for the game.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45526104/6b78058c19fc1466386a86cb0709bf2d17a06b14.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]Character Design[/h3][p]One of Supamonks’ first tasks was [b]character design[/b], and working on how our heroes are presented to the players. This is a very important step for the animation: we want just the right attention to detail for a rational time spent in animation.[/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45526104/6a28a3df5a2b7b3948c29f3a3482ab99e50cfddf.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45526104/d9de6dd6e7a7efdcf95eee43065f6e83230bf11b.jpg"][/img][/carousel][h3]Animation[/h3][p]Animation is a tricky one. You want the game to feel fluid, but you also want to make it rationally doable. If the game is too heavy on fluidity, you risk spending an unfeasible amount of time on it. At the same time, Absolum wouldn’t be as fluid as it is without the impressive amount of frames that have been created! We are extremely grateful to Leonard and his team, who rose to the challenge and found the perfect balance. [/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45526104/d9691629a0cbc44b7546e49fc13e7e1fa8379d6e.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45526104/e271a9553d4cbe62a9e4cb0ab3e694c459a7041c.jpg"][/img][/carousel][h3]FX Work[/h3][p]Pierre is our main FX artist, responsible for [b]making the design AND art of the game work perfectly together[/b]. We needed to have everyone work hand in hand to make sure the FX are placed, integrated and triggered correctly. This is extremely important, but also challenging to coordinate![/p][p][/p][h3]UI & UX Design[/h3][p]At Dotemu we have our own designer, Laurane, who also does a lot of work around the interfaces and icons produced for the game. She’s working hand in hand with both the programmer and the art director Maxime to make sure everything is consistent.
[/p][h3]Trailer Art[/h3][p]Working with an animation studio offers another great perk: it makes it that much easier to produce a truly epic trailer. We showcased it in March, and the response has been absolutely stunning: 30k wishlists in our first month! Thank you to Sebastien Iglesias for your work as trailer director on this.[/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45526104/dd4e38b4582cac47325336771a62255e221e5285.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45526104/8ef21b4a1774410475118bc1e05b0b3d2ce5efbe.png"][/img][/carousel][h3]Environment Art[/h3][p]Manuel is our main [b]environment artist[/b] and, oh boy, nothing can prepare you for the incredible amount of environment art in Absolum! notes.title: Absolum Preview — An Epic Fantasy Mash Up In The Making
notes.notes:
As a huge fan of the roguelike genre and of titles from both Dotemu and Guard Crush Games, I was eagerly awaiting the chance to get my hands on Absolum, an original beat-’em-up and a new property from the minds behind Streets of Rage 4.

Absolum is a medieval fantasy roguelike beat-’em-up featuring Dotemu’s distinct, inky and bold comic book–like aesthetic, which forgoes pixels in favour of punchy, high-fidelity art. The Steam Next Fest demo for Absolum, which I was given access to, ran for about an hour—roughly equivalent to the first major zone of the game world. Although still far from complete, the narrative in Absolum already feels compelling, with the core story focused on a world where magic has been exiled following a cataclysmic event. Players face off against the oppressive rule of the Sun King Azra, hoping to restore the world to its former magical glory.
